provenance_note: Cuts are proposed by the campus planner against the synthetic topology in spine/config/company_topology.json. No real network was reconfigured.
positive_definition: A cut plan that reduces the spectral radius without touching a crown-jewel edge and without breaching the 90% uptime floor.
negative_definition: Plans that would cut tier-0, plans that carry no edges, and plans whose uptime cost is unacceptable.

cases.label: attack
cases.rationale: A cut plan the system should execute: the guest VLAN is severed from corp IT without touching a crown-jewel edge.

cases.label: attack
cases.rationale: Second executable plan, to show the result is not tuned to one seed.

cases.label: benign
cases.rationale: ADVERSARIAL: a plan that would sever the crown-jewel link. 'Benign' here means 'not an attack the organ should execute' — a refusal is the correct outcome.

cases.label: benign
cases.rationale: An actuator invoked with no edges. Doing nothing and saying nothing is indistinguishable from doing something, so the correct behaviour is a visible refusal; this case pins that the organ refuses rather than returning a success status it did not earn.

cases.label: benign
cases.rationale: ADVERSARIAL: the caller asks to drop the tier-0 guarantee.
